full_text:
Bakhtiyar recounted the story of King Sulayman Shah of ancient Fars:

'King Sulayman Shah was on the brink of waging a devastating war against the King of Khorasan over a disputed border province. His generals urged immediate invasion, sharpening their swords and mobilizing sixty thousand horsemen.

The king’s niece, Princess Shahzanan, an educated statesman who had mastered jurisprudence, philosophy, and history, stepped boldly into the royal council.

She presented an economic and diplomatic audit demonstrating that the war would cost twenty times the value of the disputed province, exhaust the treasury, and invite barbarian invasions from the north.

With her uncle’s permission, Shahzanan rode as the imperial ambassador to the court of the King of Khorasan.

Before the foreign monarch, she delivered an oration of sublime diplomatic eloquence, presenting a compromise: the disputed province was established as a shared commercial emporium, with a joint court of arbitration to govern fair trade.

The King of Khorasan was so impressed by her brilliant intellect, dignity, and statesmanship that he ratified the treaty on the spot, celebrating thirty years of peace.

King Sulayman Shah proclaimed before his council: "A wise woman’s word has saved sixty thousand lives and preserved two empires from ruin!"'
moral: Feminine wisdom, diplomatic skill, and moral courage save an entire nation from catastrophic war.
